data.title: Funds Solicited Under the Organisation's Name
data.summary:
Fundraising was conducted using the organisation's name, branding or cause, directing
donations to accounts outside its control.
data.description:
Monetised campaigns behave differently from purely political ones. Revenue sustains the
operation, and the need to keep earning shapes the content towards whatever converts,
which makes the campaign more responsive and more persistent.

It also creates the strongest attribution evidence available. Payment infrastructure is
regulated and identity-bound in ways that posting is not, and a payment processor
responds to a fraud complaint from a trademark holder far faster than a platform responds
to a misinformation report.

Donors are victims here, and the organisation's handling of them affects whether they
accept the correction. A statement framed solely as protecting the brand will not reach
people who believe they gave to a cause.
data.recommendation:
* Report to the payment processor and the fundraising platform as fraud and trademark
  abuse, which is the fastest available route.
* Publish the organisation's genuine donation routes so there is an authoritative
  comparison.
* Address affected donors as people who were defrauded rather than as a reputational
  problem.
* Preserve payment identifiers; they are the strongest attribution evidence in most
  campaigns.
data.short_recommendation: Report to the payment processor as fraud; publish genuine donation routes.
